# Azure Resource Manager sql client library for Java

Azure Resource Manager sql client library for Java

For documentation on how to use this package, please see [Azure Management Libraries for Java](https://aka.ms/azsdk/java/mgmt).

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- [Java Development Kit (JDK)][jdk] with version 8 or above
- [Azure Subscription][azure_subscription]

### Adding the package to your product

[//]: # ({x-version-update-start;com.azure.resourcemanager:azure-resourcemanager-sql;current})
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>com.azure.resourcemanager</groupId>
    <artifactId>azure-resourcemanager-sql</artifactId>
    <version>2.55.0-beta.1</version>
</dependency>
```
[//]: # ({x-version-update-end})

### Include the recommended packages

Azure Management Libraries require a `TokenCredential` implementation for authentication and an `HttpClient` implementation for HTTP client.

[Azure Identity][azure_identity] package and [Azure Core Netty HTTP][azure_core_http_netty] package provide the default implementation.

### Authentication

Microsoft Entra ID token authentication relies on the [credential class][azure_identity_credentials] from [Azure Identity][azure_identity] package.

Azure subscription ID can be configured via `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
Azure tenant ID can be configured via `AZURE_TENANT_ID` environment variable.

Assuming the use of the `DefaultAzureCredential` credential class, the client can be authenticated using the following code:

```java readme-sample-authenticate
AzureProfile profile = new AzureProfile(AzureEnvironment.AZURE);
TokenCredential credential = new DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder()
    .authorityHost(profile.getEnvironment().getActiveDirectoryEndpoint())
    .build();
SqlServerManager manager = SqlServerManager
    .authenticate(credential, profile);
```

The sample code assumes global Azure. Please change `AzureEnvironment.AZURE` variable if otherwise.

See [Authentication][authenticate] for more options.

RegionCapabilitiesImpl indexes supported versions by name and returns an unmodifiable map. These are observable adaptations, not proven handwritten edits; no behavior of uncaptured shared utilities or null safety beyond shown guards is inferred.

ReplicationLinkImpl derives the database name from its resource ID and delegates refresh, delete, failover and forced failover calls. Async failovers discard results with then(). Their names and the existence of reactive methods do not establish custom LRO polling, retry or page-continuation behavior, and uncaptured transport operations were not followed.

SqlChildrenOperationsImpl requires a manager and IDs, decomposes child IDs into parent scope, and returns null for shown parentless get/list/reactive calls while synchronous delete becomes a no-op. These behaviors are visible but lack handwritten attribution; no global async consistency or complete error/cancellation guarantee is inferred.

SqlDatabaseExportRequestImpl composes export with optional storage-account/container work, creates a private container only on the shown management 404 path and propagates other errors. Managed-identity configuration clears the administrator password and uses the same identity for storage. These are concrete request/dependency choices, not proof of handwritten auth middleware or of end-to-end success when no key is returned.

SqlDatabaseForElasticPoolImpl sets location and pool ID, clears SKU, delegates staged configuration and returns the parent pool on attach.
